$comment: THE numbers of the Published Sites Performance Law (docs/experience/PUBLISHED-SITES-PERFORMANCE-LAW.md). This file is the single source: the CI gate (scripts/lighthouse-gate.mjs), the publish gate and the nightly fleet sampler all read it, so a floor can never drift between them. Budgets may only ever be LOWERED — raising one requires an ADR.

hydration.why: ADR-071. The App Router sends every page twice: once as HTML the browser paints, and once as the inline flight payload React hydrates from. Those bytes are neither markup nor a script file, and they are the ONE line that grows every time a section is added — so they get their own budget. PROVISIONAL: 41.0KB measured on / (2026-08-08) with headroom left for the trade artwork, to be ratcheted to measured+2 on the first green preview.

markup+styles.why: ADR-058 established the total: 70KB for markup and styles together, whichever file the bytes arrive in, because inlineCss puts the CSS inside the document. ADR-071 finishes the thought — `markup` is now the document MINUS its inline hydration payload, because a budget named markup+styles must not be billed for React's flight data. Measured 34.3KB on / (2026-08-08): half the budget spare.

scriptLaw.$comment: ADR-071. The old law wrote one number — script <= 130KB — and no page in TITAN has ever met it, because ~195KB is what Next.js App Router costs before TITAN writes a line. A ceiling nothing can reach is not a law, it is a permanently red light, and a permanently red light teaches everyone to ignore gates. So the line is split into the part TITAN does not control (measured, ratchet-down) and the part it does (budgeted, tight).

frameworkBaseline.evidence: The identical 11-chunk set on /, /about, /advertising and /privacy — 194.6KB on each, ZERO page-unique bytes. /privacy is a page of legal text and ships exactly what the home page with its sphere ships. Corroborated by the 2026-07-28 measurement of /sites/summit-roofing-rescue at 195.057KB: a different page, six weeks earlier, the same number to within half a kilobyte.
frameworkBaseline.rule: This is a MEASUREMENT, never a choice. It may only ever be re-recorded DOWNWARD — and only with a fresh measurement in the diff. Raising it requires an ADR, exactly like raising a budget.

appAuthored.why: What TITAN itself puts on the page, on top of the framework floor. Measured today: 0KB — the company site loads no client component at all, and the JS diet (ADR: CSS motion replaces framer-motion) left nothing behind. The allowance is deliberately small: 20KB buys a real island when one is genuinely needed, and trips the moment a dependency sneaks a runtime back in.
